text:
Parts of North Jakarta have sunk up to 25 cm in a year, mainly because groundwater is pumped from under homes and factories, not because of rising seas.

For anyone buying or investing in a coastal city, ground stability is a hidden risk: about 40% of Jakarta already sits below sea level, and Indonesia is spending on both sea walls and a new capital, Nusantara, which about 10,000 people have moved to so far against a plan of 1.2 million.

Sources: BBC and Bandung Institute of Technology research (2018), ABC News (Oct 2026).

Fix the sinking city, or build a new one: which would you choose?
